Q1: Britain. A flag with a red cross on a white field and a small union canton flies on the tower in frames 22-25, dated 4-5 Aug 1704, and the chapter title reads '1704 — The Rock changes hands'. The pictures don't show which nation held it before. I can't make out the flag's details at this size, so I'm inferring Britain from the red-and-white design.
Q2: The 'Great Siege' (chapter title '1779 — The Great Siege', frame 43). Wooden siege lines and forts are built across the flat land north of the rock, and ships gather offshore in July 1779.
Q3: The town is cut off. A line of lines or forts closes the land side (frames 43-48), and ships blockade the sea side (frames 49-51, 54-59). Frames 52-53 show a man and woman picking plants on a hillside in Jan 1780, which suggests food was short. There is also fire and bombardment in the town in Apr 1781 (frames 60-61) and ruins by 1782 (frames 64-67). The pictures never show an explicit cause such as an empty storehouse, so the blockade is my best reading.
Q4: Not sure. Ships appear near the rock in Jan 1780 (frame 54) and Apr 1781 (frame 59), and they could be a relief fleet. I can't tell from the pictures whether they are friendly or enemy.
Q5: A large attack from the sea. On 8 Sep 1782 there is heavy smoke and fire along the land front. A row of floating batteries or ships then lines up in front of the rock on 11-13 Sep. They burn brightly at night on 13-14 Sep (frames 86-88), so the attack on the rock seems to fail with the ships on fire.
Q6: Over time the sandy flat land is built up. Wooden lines and forts come first (1731-1783). Then it is mostly empty grass and sand through the 1800s. Small buildings and streets appear around 1904-1910, and the chapter title '1939 — A runway on the sand' marks an airstrip. Housing and a dense modern town fill the land by 1969-2026, and a runway is still visible in 2026.
Q7: Not sure. Frames 147-151 are dated Jun 1969, Aug 1969, Aug 1973, Mar 1980 and Sep 1984. They show a long line across the flat land that looks like a fence or border, and the new town grows beside it over those years. The pictures don't show a gate closing or reopening, or any people or traffic at a gate.
Q8: The runway. In the 2026 frames (155-157, 167-169) people walk across a crossing and the flat airfield, apparently on foot between the two towns. The modern streets and buildings of the two towns run up to the same strip of land. The only link the pictures clearly show is people walking across the runway or crossing, with luggage in frames 1-2.

lost.why: The opening montage jumps among 1411, 1704, 1782, 1939 and 2026 with no explanation.
A column of people and a man with a donkey walk across the plain (9-24 Aug 1704). The pictures don't say who they are or why they leave.
1729 shows a thin line on empty land and then jumps to a 2015 shot, so the timeline is unclear.
A couple picks plants on a hillside, and nothing on screen says this means hunger.
Ships come to the town in 1781, and I can't tell whether they are rescuers or attackers.
Two figures stand in a narrow street in 1910, with no clue to the point.
The 1969 shots show no gate, closure or crowd, only a faint line across the land.
The film jumps among 1735, 1943, 2026, 1731 and 1783 at the end, which confuses the order of events.
